name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,554

clue.text: Half-cut state on wine that adds flavour when cooking

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the herb rather than a noun

indicators.note: cut in half means only the first half of the state's name survives

blocks.note: a US state, of which only the front half is kept

explanation.surface: A tipsy cook pours wine into the pot to liven up the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so the half-state follows the wine. 'Half-cut' looks like drunk, but it trims Maryland.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic herb used to season roasts and other cooked dishes.

clue.text: Leader is poorly understood

indicators.note: done poorly, the words are put together badly and their letters fall out of order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss whose instructions are constantly misinterpreted by staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To have realised something is to have grasped or comprehended it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Faces of Spanish expats possess intensely attractive colour

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so each following word gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: Spaniards living abroad have a vivid, alluring complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown tint, familiar from old photographs and once made from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Strike over individual ruling? Something schoolteachers must do

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word for strike reads backwards

blocks.note: to ram is to strike hard

explanation.surface: A single ruler striking something, followed by a question about teachers' duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers spend evenings grading pupils' homework and exam papers, which is marking.

clue.text: Contracts essentially null and void for motorway, perhaps

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letter of contracts is kept
made void, the word and is emptied of its inside, leaving its two ends

explanation.surface: Legal agreements cancelled for a motorway building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Null and void' reads as a legal phrase, but null is a zero and void empties the word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorway is one example of a road, hence the 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Seller of very little scrap gold

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very; little hints at shortening
an end is a leftover fragment, as in odds and ends

explanation.surface: A dealer offering only a tiny piece of gold for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry and is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is a person who offers goods for sale, such as a street trader.

clue.text: Second person carrying rejected travel permit becomes shifty

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the travel document is read backwards
the second person holds the other piece inside, as a bearer carries a load

blocks.note: in Genesis Eve was the second human created, after Adam
an entry permit stamped in a passport

explanation.surface: Someone whose visa application is turned down starts acting suspiciously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second person' suggests grammar (you), but it is Eve, the second human in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive behaviour dodges straight answers, just as a shifty person avoids being pinned down.

clue.text: Reputational damage in party, mostly concerning Democrat appeal

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the party word is dropped

blocks.note: it as in sex appeal, charm

explanation.surface: A political party's image suffers over a Democrat's plea.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for appeal or charisma is an old usage, as in the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Discredit is loss of good name or standing, harm to how others regard someone.

clue.text: Note round variety of apple

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the banknote word is read backwards

blocks.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A short remark about a type of apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music or a memo, but it is a banknote. Rennet is better known as the curdling agent in cheesemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet, from French reinette, is also the name of several old dessert apple cultivars.

clue.text: Read an MP's novel, it's set in Bosnia & Herzegovina, for instance

definitions.text: it's set in Bosnia & Herzegovina, for instance

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Recommending a politician's book set in the Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'set in Bosnia' build a picture of a book; in fact 'set in' is literal, since the symbol sits in the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The & sign is called an ampersand, and it appears printed in the name Bosnia & Herzegovina.

clue.text: Got up without notice to speak directly to journalist

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word for notice is taken out of the next piece

blocks.note: to address someone is to speak to them

explanation.surface: Someone rose unannounced to confront a reporter face to face.
explanation.definitionFit: To be got up in something is to be clothed or costumed in it.

clue.text: Crime clerics uncovered

indicators.note: with its covering stripped, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing by the clergy exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Character inclined to be kept within hospital ICU

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A sick person likely to be detained in intensive care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character inclined' reads as a person with a tendency; it is a slanted typeface letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so an italic letter is a printed symbol leaning over.

clue.text: Foreign father receiving taunt against European parentage

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the father word holds the taunt inside it

explanation.surface: An immigrant dad mocked about his European family background.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedigree means lineage or ancestry, the line of descent from one's forebears.

clue.text: Grand estate is designed for West Sussex town

indicators.note: something designed is planned and laid out anew, so the letters get a new layout

blocks.note: taken as written, completing the fodder

explanation.surface: A stately home has been planned out for a southern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: East Grinstead is a market town in West Sussex, south of London; 'is' does double work here as part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: East Grinstead is a real market town in the English county of West Sussex.

clue.text: Sort of pay hard for African politicians to accept? On the contrary

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece is held inside the other
it flips the roles, so it is the hard word that takes in the politicians

blocks.note: the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Is a pay package too tough for South African politicians to swallow?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'On the contrary' reverse the containment: the hard word holds the party, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Severance pay is compensation given to an employee whose job is terminated.

clue.text: Arranging flowers in Tokyo store to welcome group shortly

indicators.note: cut short means losing the last letter of the group word
welcoming means taking a guest inside, so the store holds the other piece

explanation.surface: A Tokyo shop putting on a floral display to greet a visiting party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the traditional Japanese art of composing cut flowers and branches.

clue.text: Enduring restricted times for lying outside

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the first word surrounds the next

explanation.surface: Putting up with limited hours for lying in the sun, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: External describes something situated on the exterior, beyond the boundary of a thing.

clue.text: Duty of conservationist at heart

blocks.note: surface reading: an environmentalist's deepest sense of obligation
setter's reading: the three letters in the middle of the word conservationist are the initials of a tax, so the duty is that tax written in full

explanation.surface: An environmentalist's deepest sense of obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of conservationist is VAT, the everyday abbreviation of the answer, so the clue defines the tax by where its initials are hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Value-added tax is a levy on goods and services, and a duty is a tax payable to government.

clue.text: Hangs around spreading rotten lies putting cardinal down

indicators.note: putting something down suppresses it, so the cardinal is removed
completes putting down, meaning the number is taken out
spread about, the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lingers, spreading nasty falsehoods and belittling a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman but here it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loiters lingers idly in one place without obvious purpose.

clue.text: This one overheard rumour Extra Time isn't available?

definitions.note: the answer is what did the overhearing

indicators.note: what is unavailable is absent, so those words' letters are taken out

blocks.note: taken as written; the removals strip exactly its outer letters, so the result also lies hidden in this phrase, no coincidence
over means extra or left over

explanation.surface: Hearsay picked up about a match with no added period of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra Time' looks like a sporting phrase, but it splits into two words that are struck out of the first phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound, so it is what overheard.

clue.text: Build up a company, reportedly

indicators.note: reports are spoken, so the word is judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: a crew is a company of workers

explanation.surface: A business said to be expanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest or debts accrue, meaning they accumulate gradually over time.

clue.text: Chanteuse originally modelling a daring article of clothing

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its start, so only its opening letter is taken
modelling is shaping material, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A singer posing in a risqué outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modelling a daring article of clothing' reads as a fashion shoot; 'modelling' actually reshapes the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted woollen jacket fastening down the front, a garment.

clue.text: Broken coffee beans, say, occasionally man is extremely reluctant to send back

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter of the phrase is kept
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those are taken
sending back returns things the way they came, so the whole string runs backwards

explanation.surface: A man reluctant to return a bag of broken coffee beans.
explanation.walkthrough: Triage is best known as medical sorting of patients, but its older sense is the lowest-grade coffee of broken beans.
explanation.definitionFit: In the coffee trade, triage is refuse coffee made of broken beans sorted out from good ones.

clue.text: Agree flying regularly stops American being discontented

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter of flying is kept
a stopper plugs a gap, so these letters fill the middle of the other piece
with its contents gone, only the outer letters of American remain

explanation.surface: Concurring that regular flights stop because a US traveller is unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: To align with someone is to side with or come into agreement with them.

clue.text: Box southpaw, finally switching to right

indicators.note: the last letter is swapped for the letter named next

blocks.note: split as south, S, and paw, PAW

explanation.surface: A boxing coach telling a left-handed fighter to change to an orthodox stance.
explanation.walkthrough: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, which fits the boxing picture, but the word is read as two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box for practice, trading light punches with a partner.

clue.text: Distance raced needs good energy

explanation.surface: Running far takes plenty of stamina.
explanation.definitionFit: Range is the maximum reach or extent something can travel or cover.

clue.text: "Idiot," Iranian once declared to be slander

indicators.note: something declared is said out loud, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: an ass is a fool; Persian is the former name for an Iranian

explanation.surface: Calling an Iranian an idiot is declared defamatory.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions is to make damaging remarks about someone's character, a form of defamation.

clue.text: Quits job, taking away tips nevertheless

indicators.note: removing the tips means losing both ends, leaving only the centre

blocks.note: being quits means owing nothing, all square

explanation.surface: Someone resigns despite losing their gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits job' reads as resigning; quits is in fact the adjective meaning square.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is an idiom meaning however, or in spite of that.

clue.text: Credit setter's given in Alabama is deplorable

blocks.note: the setter is, from the setter's point of view

explanation.surface: A setter's reputation in Alabama is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal is used informally to mean shameful or disgraceful, as in a criminal waste.
